Short answer: when notifications are lost while a user is offline, debug the durable record and cursor before the live connection. For a financial chat room that must survive reconnects, commit each notification to an ordered room log before attempting best-effort publish. Give the client a room-scoped read token, require it to acknowledge a monotonic cursor, and replay everything after that cursor when it reconnects. This is the least complex design that makes an offline gap explainable.
Start with the delivery contract.



Contract
Pick this when
Offline behavior
Client trust boundary




Ephemeral publish
Typing or presence can disappear
Nothing is recovered
Client observes only the live room


Durable room log plus cursor
Every chat notification must appear after reconnect
Replay after…

Project Pulse is a magnetic vibration/sound probe for small motors — fans, pumps, compressors, conveyor drives. Snap it onto a running machine and in about 30 seconds it tells you the ISO severity zone, the likely fault (imbalance, looseness, overload, bearing wear), and what to check, in plain language instead of a wall of numbers. articles.description:
I wanted to see where my money went each month without uploading my bank data anywhere or maintaining a spreadsheet. So I built Finoinc.
Export the .ofx statement your bank already offers and drop it in. Finoinc skips what you already imported, pairs charges with their refunds, applies your rules and lays the month out on a dashboard.

Rules categorize every import, and the app points out recurring charges that still have no rule
Card bills and transfers between your own accounts don't count twice
Bills on a calendar: paid, pending, overdue
Investments tracked apart from spending
Optional local MCP server, so an AI agent can answer questions about your money


Everything lives in one SQLite file on your Mac. No account, no telemetry, no network calls by default.

Free and open source (MIT), built with Tauri, Svelte and Rust. macOS 12+, Apple Silicon and Intel.
Site: https://mateusfonsek.github.io/finoinc/

Code: https://github.com/mateusfonsek/finoinc



Feedback welcome.
articles.title: Finoinc: local-first personal finance for macOS

articles.author: Yuri Peixinho
articles.description:
Introdução


TDD (Test-Driven Development, ou Desenvolvimento Guiado por Testes) inverte a ordem natural de escrever código: em vez de implementar a funcionalidade e só depois escrever testes para confirmar que ela funciona, você escreve o teste primeiro — um teste que falha, porque o código que ele exercita ainda nem existe — e só então escreve o código mínimo necessário para fazer esse teste passar.
Essa inversão parece pequena, mas muda tudo. Quando você testa depois, o teste normalmente confirma o que o código já faz — inclusive os vícios de design que ele carrega. Quando você testa antes, o teste é quem dita como o código deveria ser usado: sua API, suas dependências, seus pontos de extensão. O teste vira uma especificação executável, não uma rede de segurança criada depois do fato.
T…
